item.title: Democrats Sweep the Midterms, Taking the House, Senate, and Five Governorships
item.description:
Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in Tuesday's midterm elections, delivering a repudiation of President Donald Trump that will force divided government for the final two years of his term. The party flipped at least seven Senate seats — only four were needed for the majority — and at least 25 House seats, with California's redistricting alone netting five more Democratic representatives.

The blue wave extended well beyond Congress. Democrats flipped five governorships — in Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Iowa, and Nevada — and now hold 28 of the 50 governorships, their first majority since 2010. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton for the Senate seat while Gina Hinojosa beat Governor Greg Abbott; in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed became the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator. A few races in Alaska, Kansas, and Mississippi were still uncalled as of Wednesday evening, but the balance of power is settled: Democrats control Washington's legislature and a majority of statehouses going into 2027.

Sources

  • The Pour Over: Morning after Midterms

item.title: Midterm Eve: the stage is set for Tuesday's elections
item.description:
The Pour Over's Midterm Eve edition sets the stage for Tuesday's midterm elections. As the campaign season's final day arrives, the newsletter rounds up where things stand heading into voting day — the races to watch, the stakes as each side frames them, and what the results could mean for the balance of power in Washington.

It's the calm-before-the-storm edition: a last, clear-eyed look at the map before the votes are counted and the spin begins.
